            await github.rest.issues.createComment({
              owner: process.env.TARGET_OWNER, repo: process.env.TARGET_REPO,
              issue_number: Number(process.env.TRIGGER_ISSUE_NUMBER),
              body: `${require(`${process.env.RUNTIME_DIR}/scripts/project-link.cjs`).projectLink(process.env)}\n\nRestored app is ready. New changes are not yet verified.`
            });
      - name: Run OpenCode and locate its web session
        id: opencode_run
        if: env.SSH_ONLY_REQUEST != 'true'
        shell: bash
        working-directory: ${{ env.PROJECT_DIR }}
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          OPENCODE_WEB_URL: ${{ steps.opencode_web.outputs.url }}
          OPENCODE_MODEL: ${{ steps.opencode_labels.outputs.model }}
          OPENCODE_MODELS_JSON: ${{ steps.opencode_labels.outputs.models_json }}
          OPENCODE_MODEL_ROUTES_JSON: ${{ steps.opencode_labels.outputs.routes_json }}
          OPENCODE_VARIANT: ${{ steps.opencode_labels.outputs.variant }}
          OPENCODE_SKILLS: ${{ steps.opencode_labels.outputs.skills_json }}
          GOAL_REQUEST: ${{ env.GOAL_REQUEST }}
          RALPH_REQUEST: ${{ env.RALPH_REQUEST }}
          OMO_REQUEST: ${{ env.OMO_REQUEST }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "$TEST_REQUEST" == 'true' ]]; then
            /usr/bin/time -p node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/seed-test-session.mjs"
            RESUME_SESSION_ID="$(cat "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/synthetic-session-id")"
            printf '%s\n' fixture > "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/main-model"
          else
          OPENCODE_BIN="$HOME/.opencode/bin/opencode"
          PROMPT_FILE="$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/prompt.txt"
          RUN_LOG="$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/opencode-run.log"
          RUN_EXIT="$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/opencode-run.exit"
          printf '%s\n' "$OPENCODE_MODEL" > "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/main-model"
          if [[ -n "${RESUME_SESSION_ID:-}" ]]; then
            printf '%s' "$COMMENT_BODY" > "$PROMPT_FILE"
          else
            skill_text="$(jq -r 'if length == 0 then "(none)" else join(", ") end' <<<"$OPENCODE_SKILLS")"
            prompt_template="$(< "$RUNTIME_DIR/.github/prompts/01-build.md")"
            request_text="$COMMENT_BODY"
            prompt="${prompt_template//@COMMENT_BODY@/$request_text}"
            prompt="${prompt//@OPENCODE_MODEL@/$OPENCODE_MODEL}"
            prompt="${prompt//@SKILL_TEXT@/$skill_text}"
            printf '%s\n' "$prompt" > "$PROMPT_FILE"
          fi
          nohup node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/run-with-model-fallback.mjs" \
            "$OPENCODE_BIN" "$OPENCODE_WEB_PORT" "$PROMPT_FILE" "$RUN_LOG" "$RUN_EXIT" "$OPENCODE_MODEL" \
            > /dev/null 2>&1 &
          echo $! > "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/opencode-run.pid"
          fi
          SESSION_ID="${RESUME_SESSION_ID:-}"
          for _ in {1..120}; do
            [[ "$SESSION_ID" == ses_* ]] && break
            SESSION_ID="$(node -e 'const fs=require("fs");try { for(const line of fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8").split("\n")) { try { const row=JSON.parse(line); if(/^ses_[A-Za-z0-9]+$/.test(row.sessionID||"")) { process.stdout.write(row.sessionID); break } } catch {} } } catch {}' "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/opencode-run.log")"

            [[ "$SESSION_ID" == ses_* ]] && break
            [[ -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/opencode-run.exit" ]] && { tail -40 "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/opencode-run.log" >&2; break; }
            sleep 1
          done
          [[ "$SESSION_ID" == ses_* ]]
          /usr/bin/time -p printf '%s\n' "$SESSION_ID" > "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/checkpoint-session-id"
          /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail --silent "http://127.0.0.1:$OPENCODE_CONTROL_PORT/omgithub/heartbeat"
          /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail --silent "http://127.0.0.1:$OPENCODE_CONTROL_PORT/omgithub/reconcile"
          SESSION_URL="$(node --input-type=module -e "import { v2SessionUrl } from '$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/opencode-v2-api.mjs';console.log(v2SessionUrl(process.argv[1],process.argv[2]))" "$OPENCODE_WEB_URL" "$SESSION_ID")"

          printf 'session_id=%s\nsession_url=%s\n' "$SESSION_ID" "$SESSION_URL" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Post temporary access details
        id: access_comment
        if: env.SSH_ONLY_REQUEST != 'true'
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        env:
          AGENTSWEB_SSH_ENABLED: ${{ env.AGENTSWEB_SSH_ENABLED }}
          AGENTSWEB_SSH_READY: ${{ steps.agentsweb.outcome == 'success' }}
          EARLY_SSH_COMMENT_ID: ${{ steps.agentsweb.outputs.comment_id }}
          SSH_ACCESS_FILE: ${{ runner.temp }}/omgithub-ssh/access.env
          SSH_TUNNEL_LOG: ${{ runner.temp }}/omgithub-ssh/tunnel.log
        with:
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          script: |
            require(`${process.env.RUNTIME_DIR}/.github/scripts/github-rate-observer.cjs`).attach(github, process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR);
            const fs = require('node:fs');
            const sshReady = process.env.AGENTSWEB_SSH_ENABLED === 'true' &&
              process.env.AGENTSWEB_SSH_READY === 'true' &&
              fs.existsSync(process.env.SSH_ACCESS_FILE);
            const access = sshReady
              ? Object.fromEntries(fs.readFileSync(process.env.SSH_ACCESS_FILE, 'utf8').trim().split('\n').map((line) => {
                  const separator = line.indexOf('=');
                  return [line.slice(0, separator), line.slice(separator + 1)];
                }))
              : {};
            const tunnelLog = fs.existsSync(process.env.SSH_TUNNEL_LOG)
              ? fs.readFileSync(process.env.SSH_TUNNEL_LOG, 'utf8')
              : '';
            const tunnelUrl = access.AGENTSWEB_TUNNEL_URL ||
              (tunnelLog.match(/^ssh:\/\/[^\s]+/m) || [])[0] ||
              'not registered';
            const number = Number(process.env.TRIGGER_ISSUE_NUMBER);
            const run = `https://github.com/${context.repo.owner}/${context.repo.repo}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`;
            const sshSection = sshReady
              ? [
                  '🔐 **Temporary AgentsWeb SSH session is ready.**', '',
                  `Run: ${run}`, `SSH URL: \`${tunnelUrl}\``, `Host: \`${access.AGENTSWEB_HOST}:${access.AGENTSWEB_PORT}\``, '',
                  'Run this command while the job is active:', '',
                  '```sh', access.AGENTSWEB_COMMAND, '```'
                ].join('\n')
              : (process.env.AGENTSWEB_SSH_ENABLED === 'true'
                ? ['⚠️ **AgentsWeb SSH tunnel setup failed.**', '', `Run: ${run}`, `SSH URL: \`${tunnelUrl}\``].join('\n')
                : '');
            const body = [sshSection,
              process.env.FUSION_ACCESS_TOKEN
                ? `Fusion plugin: \`${/^[a-f0-9]{40}$/.test(String(process.env.FUSION_PLUGIN_COMMIT || '')) ? process.env.FUSION_PLUGIN_COMMIT : 'unavailable'}\``
                : '',
              require(`${process.env.RUNTIME_DIR}/scripts/project-link.cjs`).projectLink(process.env),
              process.env.TEST_REQUEST === 'true'
                ? 'This is a synthetic OpenCode session for the full workflow test.'
                : 'Open the project to access chat, live files, previews, and progress.'
            ].filter(Boolean).join('\n\n');
            const earlyComment = Number(process.env.EARLY_SSH_COMMENT_ID);
            const comment = earlyComment
              ? await github.rest.issues.updateComment({ owner: process.env.TARGET_OWNER, repo: process.env.TARGET_REPO, comment_id: earlyComment, body })
              : await github.rest.issues.createComment({ owner: process.env.TARGET_OWNER, repo: process.env.TARGET_REPO, issue_number: number, body });
            core.setOutput('comment_id', comment.data.id);
      - name: Wait for main OpenCode completion
        if: env.TEST_REQUEST != 'true' && env.SSH_ONLY_REQUEST != 'true'
        shell: bash
        run: |-
          set -euo pipefail
          /usr/bin/time -p node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/runner-watch.mjs" build
          if [[ "$(cat "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/opencode-run.exit")" != 0 ]]; then
            /usr/bin/time -p node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/run-failure.mjs" --summary >&2
            exit 1
          fi
      - name: Wait for production delivery
        if: env.SSH_ONLY_REQUEST != 'true'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          /usr/bin/time -p node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/wait-deployment.mjs"
      - name: Create OpenCode logs release
        continue-on-error: true
        if: always() && env.SSH_ONLY_REQUEST != 'true' && steps.opencode_run.outcome == 'success'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          release_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/opencode-release"
          mkdir -p "$release_dir"

          # Preserve machine-readable responses and execution logs without
          # publishing OpenCode configuration, credentials, or SSH material.
          /usr/bin/time -p node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/log-response.mjs" "$release_dir/opencode-response.json"
          if [[ ! -s "$release_dir/opencode-response.json" ]]; then
            echo 'OpenCode response artifact is empty; refusing to create an incomplete release.' >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          for artifact in "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR"/*.log "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR"/model-attempts.json "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR"/main-model "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR"/fusion-plugin-commit.txt; do
            [[ -f "$artifact" && -s "$artifact" ]] || continue
            [[ "$(basename "$artifact")" == 'opencode.json' ]] && continue
            cp -f "$artifact" "$release_dir/"
          done

          release_assets=()
          for asset in "$release_dir"/*; do
            [[ -f "$asset" && -s "$asset" ]] || continue
            release_assets+=("$asset")
          done
          ((${#release_assets[@]} > 0))

          tag="opencode-logs-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          gh release create "$tag" "${release_assets[@]}" \
            --target "$TARGET_SHA" \
            --title "OpenCode logs for run #${GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER}" \
            --notes "Generated OpenCode response and execution logs for workflow run [#${GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER}](https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID})." \
            --latest=false
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      - name: Mark issue waiting for reply
        if: success() && env.SSH_ONLY_REQUEST != 'true' && env.AWAITING_REPLY_ENDED == 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          retries: 3
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          script: |
            require(`${process.env.RUNTIME_DIR}/.github/scripts/github-rate-observer.cjs`).attach(github, process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR);
            const number = Number(process.env.TRIGGER_ISSUE_NUMBER);
            const warn = (error) => core.warning(error.message);
            await github.rest.issues.createComment({
              owner: process.env.TARGET_OWNER, repo: process.env.TARGET_REPO, issue_number: number,
              body: 'OpenCode asked a question and is waiting for your reply. The session ended; open the game on OmGithub and use Continue to answer.'
            }).catch(warn);
            for (const name of ['in progress', 'validating']) await github.rest.issues.removeLabel({
              owner: process.env.TARGET_OWNER, repo: process.env.TARGET_REPO, issue_number: number, name
            }).catch((error) => { if (error.status !== 404) warn(error); });
      - name: Mark issue complete
        if: success() && env.SSH_ONLY_REQUEST != 'true' && env.AWAITING_REPLY_ENDED != 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          retries: 3
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          script: |
            require(`${process.env.RUNTIME_DIR}/.github/scripts/github-rate-observer.cjs`).attach(github, process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR);
            const number = Number(process.env.TRIGGER_ISSUE_NUMBER);
            await github.rest.issues.removeLabel({
              owner: process.env.TARGET_OWNER, repo: process.env.TARGET_REPO,
              issue_number: number, name: 'in progress'
            }).catch((error) => { if (error.status !== 404) throw error; });
            await github.rest.issues.removeLabel({
              owner: process.env.TARGET_OWNER, repo: process.env.TARGET_REPO,
              issue_number: number, name: 'validating'
            }).catch((error) => { if (error.status !== 404) throw error; });
            await github.rest.issues.addLabels({
              owner: process.env.TARGET_OWNER, repo: process.env.TARGET_REPO,
              issue_number: number, labels: ['complete']
            });
      - name: Mark issue failed
        if: failure()
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          retries: 3
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          script: |
            require(`${process.env.RUNTIME_DIR}/.github/scripts/github-rate-observer.cjs`).attach(github, process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR);
            const number = Number(process.env.TRIGGER_ISSUE_NUMBER);
            const runUrl = `https://github.com/${process.env.TARGET_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`;
            const warn = (error) => core.warning(error.message);
            await github.rest.issues.createComment({
              owner: process.env.TARGET_OWNER,
              repo: process.env.TARGET_REPO,
              issue_number: number,
              body: `Build failed. [Open workflow logs](${runUrl}).`
            }).catch(warn);
            await github.rest.issues.removeLabel({
              owner: process.env.TARGET_OWNER, repo: process.env.TARGET_REPO,
              issue_number: number, name: 'in progress'
            }).catch((error) => { if (error.status !== 404) warn(error); });
            await github.rest.issues.removeLabel({
              owner: process.env.TARGET_OWNER, repo: process.env.TARGET_REPO,
              issue_number: number, name: 'validating'
            }).catch((error) => { if (error.status !== 404) warn(error); });
            await github.rest.issues.addLabels({
              owner: process.env.TARGET_OWNER, repo: process.env.TARGET_REPO,
              issue_number: number, labels: ['failed']
            }).catch(warn);
      - name: Report failed build before debug hold
        if: failure()
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        env:
          OMGITHUB_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN || 'https://omgithub.com' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sequence=$(/usr/bin/time -p node -p 'Date.now()')
          payload="{\"run\":\"$GITHUB_RUN_ID\",\"attempt\":$GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT,\"sequence\":$sequence,\"state\":\"ended\",\"phase\":\"building\",\"outcome\":\"failure\",\"reason\":\"The build workflow failed before model diagnostics were available. Open the workflow logs for details.\"}"
          if [[ -f "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/run-failure.mjs" ]]; then
            payload=$(/usr/bin/time -p node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/run-failure.mjs" --payload "$sequence")
          fi
          /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error --retry 2 --retry-all-errors --max-time 15 \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $OMGITHUB_CALLBACK_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
            --data "$payload" \
            "$OMGITHUB_ORIGIN/api/github/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$TRIGGER_ISSUE_NUMBER/run"
      - name: Release account credentials before debug hold
        if: always() && env.AGENTSWEB_SSH_ENABLED != 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ -f "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/account-credentials.mjs" ]]; then
            /usr/bin/time -p node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/account-credentials.mjs" finish
          fi
      - name: Keep preview until one hour idle
        if: (success() || (failure() && vars.OPENCODE_DEBUG_HOLD == 'true' && steps.opencode_web.outcome == 'success')) && env.TEST_REQUEST != 'true' && env.SSH_ONLY_REQUEST != 'true' && env.AWAITING_REPLY_ENDED != 'true'
        shell: bash
        run: |-
          set -euo pipefail
          /usr/bin/time -p node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/runner-watch.mjs" preview
      - name: Sync and release account credentials
        if: always()
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/omgithub-account-auth-sync.pid" ]]; then
            /usr/bin/time -p kill "$(cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/omgithub-account-auth-sync.pid")" 2>/dev/null || true
          fi
          if [[ -f "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/account-credentials.mjs" ]]; then
            /usr/bin/time -p node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/account-credentials.mjs" release
          fi
      - name: Stop lifecycle controller
        if: always() && env.SSH_ONLY_REQUEST != 'true' && steps.opencode_run.outcome == 'success'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          /usr/bin/time -p node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/stop-lifecycle.mjs"
      - name: Append SSH session closed
        if: always() && env.AGENTSWEB_SSH_ENABLED == 'true' && steps.agentsweb.outcome == 'success' && (steps.agentsweb.outputs.comment_id != '' || steps.access_comment.outputs.comment_id != '' || steps.ssh_access_comment.outputs.comment_id != '')
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          script: |
            require(`${process.env.RUNTIME_DIR}/.github/scripts/github-rate-observer.cjs`).attach(github, process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR);
            const { renderTemplate } = require(`${process.env.RUNTIME_DIR}/.github/scripts/opencode-comment-templates.cjs`);
            await github.rest.issues.createComment({
              owner: process.env.TARGET_OWNER, repo: process.env.TARGET_REPO,
              issue_number: Number(process.env.TRIGGER_ISSUE_NUMBER),
              body: renderTemplate('opencode-ssh-closed-comment.md', {
                RUN_NUMBER: context.runNumber,
                RUN_URL: `https://github.com/${context.repo.owner}/${context.repo.repo}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`
              })
            });
      - name: Clean up OpenCode session
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set +e
          if [[ -f "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/stop-lifecycle.mjs" ]]; then
            /usr/bin/time -p node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/stop-lifecycle.mjs"
          fi
          if [[ -f "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/worker-tunnel.mjs" ]]; then
            /usr/bin/time -p node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/worker-tunnel.mjs" stop
          fi
          [[ -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/frpc.pid" ]] && kill "$(cat "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/frpc.pid")" 2>/dev/null || true
          [[ -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/live-files.pid" ]] && /usr/bin/time -p kill "$(cat "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/live-files.pid")" 2>/dev/null || true
          [[ -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/opencode.pid" ]] && kill "$(cat "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/opencode.pid")" 2>/dev/null || true
          [[ -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/opencode-run.pid" ]] && kill "$(cat "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/opencode-run.pid")" 2>/dev/null || true
          [[ -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/app.pid" ]] && kill "$(cat "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/app.pid")" 2>/dev/null || true
          tmux kill-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null || true
          [[ -f "$SSH_DIR/tunnel.pid" ]] && kill "$(cat "$SSH_DIR/tunnel.pid")" 2>/dev/null || true
          [[ -f "$SSH_DIR/sshd.pid" ]] && sudo kill "$(cat "$SSH_DIR/sshd.pid")" 2>/dev/null || true
          sudo pkill -f 'sshd.*2222' 2>/dev/null || true
          rm -f "$SSH_KEY" "$SSH_PUBLIC_KEY"
          rm -rf "$SSH_DIR" "$HOME/.ssh/authorized_keys"
          rm -rf "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR"
      - name: Report terminal build status
        if: always()
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          OMGITHUB_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN || 'https://omgithub.com' }}
          OUTCOME: ${{ job.status == 'success' && env.AWAITING_REPLY_ENDED == 'true' && 'awaiting_reply' || job.status }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          sequence=$(/usr/bin/time -p node -p 'Date.now()')
          /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error --retry 2 --retry-all-errors --max-time 15 \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $OMGITHUB_CALLBACK_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
            --data "{\"run\":\"$GITHUB_RUN_ID\",\"attempt\":$GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT,\"sequence\":$sequence,\"state\":\"ended\",\"phase\":\"building\",\"outcome\":\"$OUTCOME\"}" \
            "$OMGITHUB_ORIGIN/api/github/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$TRIGGER_ISSUE_NUMBER/run"
    needs: prepare
    if: needs.prepare.outputs.approved == 'true'

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Morning Mayhem — Dad Duty

A single-file browser RPG about getting three kids through a busy morning. Open `index.html` (or run `npm run serve`) and press **Start game**.

- **Move:** WASD / arrow keys / on-screen pad

**Backyard breather:** walk Dad into the exit door (or interact with it) and confirm to head outside. Given their desire for "actual interactive outside games" rather than text dialogs, we should design mini-games in the yard:
1. **Fetch minigame**: Charlie drops a ball; a moving target ring, Dad must position near the ball and throw (timing/power). Could be canvas interaction: ball arcs, Charlie chases; player moves to catch/throw. Simple but interactive.
2. **Sandbox building**: drag/tap to place sand blocks? Or a stacking timing game: tap when meter is in sweet spot to build a sandcastle, girls imitate. Maybe move Dad around collecting buckets of water/sand.
3. **Tag / hide-and-seek with the girls**: girls scatter; Dad must find/tag each within time; using proximity, line-of-sight? Hide in trees/sandbox. Rewards mood/history.
4. **Kite flying**: steer a kite with movement keys; avoid trees; wind gusts. Could be simple canvas physics.
5. **Scooter/bike race**: Dad races Elaina along a path? Top-down timed checkpoint course in the yard/street? Keep within fences.
6. **Garden/yard chores**: planting seeds, watering, weeding—actual mini-game with growth over days? Single-day game, maybe collect weeds and water plants, gives chores purpose and "outside work".
7. **Neighborhood walk**: walk along sidewalk with kids, teach road safety—stop at curb, hold hands, cross when clear of cars. This ties directly to cars already moving. Interactive and parenting-themed: keep girls from stepping into the street, hold hands, wait for cars.
8. **Simon-says / freeze dance**: kids mimic Dad's emotes/buttons.
9. **Sibling conflict mediation**: girls argue over sandbox toy; Dad must choose dialogue and then physically retrieve/alternate turns; not just text but a sequence of actions (give toy, set timer, redirect).
10. **Bathroom routine independence**: visual checklist with timers where Dad prompts each step; maybe too text.

Parenting simulator aspects:
- **Kid autonomy & initiative**: girls should have needs/wants (hunger, energy, hygiene, fun, attention) that decay, and they act on them autonomously. Dad can preempt or respond. Currently reactive scripted tasks.
- **Emotional states and escalation**: mood drives sibling conflicts, tantrums, dawdling; Dad can coach, distract, validate. Add "connection meter" per child that improves cooperation.
- **Consistency & follow-through**: if Dad gives a consequence, must enforce; making threats and not following through reduces trust. Add "trust/credibility" stat.
- **Routines and transitions**: warnings before transitions ("5 minutes until shoes"), visual schedule, resistance if surprised.
- **Sibling dynamics**: competition for attention; delegate to older sibling, which can build responsibility or resentment.
- **Energy/time management for Dad**: sleep, coffee, breaks; already present.
- **Consequences with memory**: girls remember bribes, promises, fairness; mood/history partly.
- **Different parenting styles** with tradeoffs: gentle/authoritative/permissive; current choices are mostly random probabilities and bribery always works. Make style have longitudinal effects—e.g., authoritarian short-term compliance but lower connection, calm slower but builds trust, bribery works but increases future bargaining, delegate builds competence for older kids but strains them.
- **Kid-specific personalities**: Elaina (12) wants autonomy, Elsie (9) fairness, Ellerle (5) imagination/needs reassurance. Current ages affect probabilities; make specific quirks and preferences.
- **Needs vs. wants**: outdoor play reduces "energy" but delays chores; screen time tradeoff; sugar; nap.
- **Natural consequences**: skipping breakfast → hunger grumpiness; skipping showers → complaints; not doing laundry → no clean clothes later. Currently tasks are just gates, no downstream effects. This is a big one for simulation feel.
- **Tantrum meter / co-regulation**: Dad's calmness affects kids. A "household temperature" that rises with chaos and lowers with connection.
- **Morning routine board**: kids independently do steps based on habit/competence, so Dad manages exceptions rather than doing everything.
- **Dad's mental load**: task list, interruptions. Already.

Interactive outdoor games (non-text, canvas mechanics):
1. **Fetch** with a throw power/timing bar: tap/click/hold to throw; Charlie chases ball; if it lands in flowerbed, Charlie rolls in mud (mess consequence—bath later). Dad can also play with girls: throw ball, they run; aim to keep all engaged. This can be built with clicks and player movement.
2. **Kite flying**: hold to run, wind gusts; keep kite above trees; girls take turns. Maybe too complex.
3. **Hide-and-seek**: countdown then search; girls hide at spots, proximity reveals rustling; tapping them tags. Charlie can "find" them, making it easier. Timer-based; if Dad takes too long, girls get bored.
4. **Sandcastle stacking**: press action at right time to pat sand; build tiers; girls add decorations; collapse if mistimed. This is a classic timing mini-game; concrete visual output (sandcastle grows) and cooperative score.
5. **Obstacle course / sack race**: place cones, run around checkpoints with each girl following; keep order, wait at finish. Could be a timed course with arrows.
6. **Red light, green light**: girls freeze/move based on Dad's call; button toggles; if caught moving, giggle and restart. Simple and social.
7. **Road safety / sidewalk walk**: hold hands (toggle) to keep girls close; cars pass; cross at crosswalk only when clear; teach waiting. This is a natural extension of the street/cars already there.
8. **Tag**: tag each girl; they scatter; Charlie joins; mood boost; tiredness consequence.
9. **Garden watering**: fill watering can at spigot, carry to plants, water before it empties; plants visually grow/perk up; maybe a daily chore that yields vegetables for dinner (ties into meal). Could be a mini-game with resource management.
10. **Neighborhood scavenger hunt**: find 3 colored objects in yard; girls call hints; visual sparkles. Too simple?
11. **Bike wash / car wash**: soap, spray, scrub via rapid taps; messy fun; clothes get wet (laundry consequence).
12. **Chalk drawing**: drag finger to draw on sidewalk; girls rate it; creative, non-competitive. This is easy to implement and genuinely interactive.
13. **Jump rope / hopscotch rhythm**: timing taps to keep rhythm; girls join; longer combo boosts mood.
14. **Bug hunt / nature journal**: catch fireflies/butterflies with net; move and time swing; release them.

For implementation scope, the most valuable and fitting:
- **Neighborhood walk / road safety** ties to cars and parenting (supervision, holding hands, waiting).
- **Sandcastle stacking** is simple, visual, and uses existing sandbox.
- **Fetch catch/throw** uses Charlie and existing fetch action, converting it from a text toast to a game.

Right now the parenting layer is mostly **dialog choice → probability roll → mood/history change**. That works, but it still feels like a task checklist with parenting-themed buttons. To feel like a parenting simulator, the house should run on **kids’ needs, attention, and consequences**, and the yard should have **things you physically do**, not dialogs that say “the girls had fun.”

## Simulation changes that would add the most depth

**1. Give each girl real needs**
Track hidden meters like `connection`, `fun`, `energy`, and `hunger`. They decay over time and drive behavior:
- Low fun → dawdling, silliness, touching things they shouldn’t.
- Low connection → following Dad around, interrupting, jealousy when he helps a sister.
- Low energy → meltdowns, slower movement, refusing transitions.
- Hunger → grumpiness that makes every request harder.

Dad sees hints through bubbles, posture, and agenda text instead of raw numbers. This turns “make breakfast” into “notice Ellerle is melting down because she’s hungry and Dad has been in the laundry room for ten minutes.”

**2. Split Dad’s attention**
The strongest parenting-sim mechanic would be that **Dad cannot supervise everywhere at once**:
- Girls in another room start arguing, making a mess, or getting into the laundry.
- A “someone needs Dad” indicator appears, and he has to physically walk over.
- Leaving two kids alone near the toys can start a sharing conflict.
- Charlie can act as an early warning: barking, nudging, or sitting by the doorway.

That creates constant small tradeoffs: finish the dishes, or intervene before the conflict escalates?

**3. Sibling dynamics and fairness**
- Elaina wants autonomy and hates being ordered around in front of her sisters.
- Elsie is sensitive to fairness and turn-taking.
- Ellerle wants reassurance and imagination.
- Delegating to Elaina can build responsibility, but too much parentification lowers her connection.
- Bribery works short-term but increases bargaining later; calm reasoning is slower but builds trust; firmness gets immediate compliance but costs connection.

Right now the four parenting styles are mostly different probabilities. They should have **different long-term curves**.

**4. Trust and follow-through**

- Warn “five more minutes,” then actually give the warning before ending play.
- If Dad threatens a consequence and doesn’t follow through, girls test boundaries more.
- If Dad promises a reward and forgets, trust drops.
- Repeated bribery makes rewards less effective.

This makes consistency a real skill rather than a dialog option.

**5. Routines that kids partly run themselves**
Instead of Dad doing every step, each girl has a morning routine: teeth, clothes, hair, shoes, bag. Older kids advance on their own; younger kids need prompts. Dad manages exceptions and reminders. This feels much more like parenting than completing a chore bar.

**6. Natural consequences instead of hard gates**
- Skipping breakfast → hunger makes the next chore harder.
- Muddy outdoor play → dirty clothes, so laundry matters later.
- Rushing a transition without a warning → meltdown and lost time.
- Ignoring a sibling conflict → both moods drop and cooperation suffers.

These aren’t instant fail states; they’re costs that show up later.

## Outdoor games that are actually playable

These would use the existing yard, sandbox, trees, girls, Charlie, and cars:

**Fetch — throw-and-chase**
- Hold to charge, release to throw.
- Ball has simple physics and bounces.

**Hide-and-seek — spatial search**
- Girls hide behind trees, the sandbox, and the fence.

- Charlie can sniff and bark near a hidden girl.
- Find everyone before the timer ends for a big bonding payoff.

**Red light, green light**
- Dad calls “green light” and the girls advance; “red light” freezes them.
- Catch someone moving and they giggle and restart.
- Simple timing/attention game that fits the yard perfectly.

**Road-safety walk**
- Hold hands with up to two girls.
- Walk the sidewalk and wait for cars before crossing.
- A girl not holding hands near the curb may dart toward the street.
- Dad has to call her back or physically reach her.
- Uses the cars already driving past and is deeply parenting-themed.

**Garden watering**
- Fill a watering can at the spigot, carry it to plants, water them before it empties.
- Plants visibly perk up; later you can harvest vegetables for dinner.
- Ties outdoor play into the household loop instead of being a separate buff stop.

**Chalk drawing**
- Drag to draw on the sidewalk.
- Girls request shapes or colors; Dad draws them.
- Low-stakes creative bonding with immediate visual feedback.

## What I’d build first

The best first slice is **sandcastle stacking + fetch physics**, because they reuse the sandbox and Charlie and turn two current text actions into tactile games. Then **hide-and-seek**, then the **road-safety walk** as the deeper parenting set piece.

A good loop would be: play → visible fun → a small real consequence (muddy dog, dirty clothes, tired kid) → Dad has to handle it later.

Currently sandbox and fetch are instant dialog choices. The user wants playable mini-games. I need to decide how to preserve existing tests while adding mini-games. The tests call `__game.playInSandbox()` and `__game.playFetch()` directly and expect immediate outcome. If I change those to launch mini-games, tests will fail unless the test suite is updated. We're allowed to update tests. But maintaining backward-compatible semantics for those debug helpers might be good. However, the goal is meaningful playable activities. The dialog choices "Play in the sandbox together" and "Play fetch with Charlie" should launch mini-games now. We can keep `playInSandbox`/`playFetch` as instant "simulate completed" helpers for debug tests, or modify them to open mini-games and update tests to complete them. Better: create new functions `startSandcastleGame()` and `startFetchGame()`, and keep `playInSandbox`/`playFetch` as legacy completion functions? That creates inconsistent UX in tests but not user-facing. Existing tests can continue passing, plus new tests for the mini-games.

But architecture matters. Let's design the mini-games to be visually rich and integrate with canvas.

Option A: In-world canvas overlay drawn on the main game canvas while paused. Use DOM overlay for instructions and result, with click/tap/keyboard input. Since pointer events on canvas are available, but dialogs currently overlay. A dedicated `.minigame-shade` div containing its own canvas could be easier to test and render: a modal that takes over the screen while playing, with touch-friendly big controls. Mobile is a priority.

Option B: Play directly in the main yard canvas, with a HUD overlay. Draw the mini-game in the lower portion / atop the yard; pointer coordinates map to canvas. But the canvas is letterboxed, coordinate mapping is doable. Mobile: tapping the action button etc. Since game already has mobile no-scroll and touch, modal with its own canvas is more reliable.

I'll go with a dedicated overlay `#minigameShade` with `#miniCanvas` (e.g. 560x420 logical) and header/instructions/progress + button. It will pause the main game. Input via pointerdown on canvas + keyboard (space/enter) for accessibility. Both games:

### Sandcastle mini-game (tap-timing)
Visual: beach sand area, a castle being built on the sand, waves in the background. A vertical "pack the sand" meter with a moving sweet-spot band. Tap/click at the right time to add a tower/tier. Needs 5 successful placements to complete 5 tiers. A hit in the green zone adds a perfect block (+score, builds taller), near miss adds a wobbly block (still counts but lower quality), complete miss collapses part / reduces quality and maybe time. The castle has 5 levels: base, walls, tower, turret, flag. Each press drops a bucket of sand. Time-limited, maybe 30s or 6 attempts. Score determines rewards.

Implementation detail: Use requestAnimationFrame loop specific to mini-game, with its own state. The main game loop still runs but is paused via a `miniGame` flag checked in `step` (avoid progress/elapsed). Actually main `step` currently runs `draw()` and updates UI. If paused via a local flag, step does `if(started&&!ended&&!paused)` logic. We can set `paused=true` when mini-game open. But `step` also calls draw; while mini-game overlay is over it, fine. `updateUI()` still runs. If paused=true, game logic won't run. The mini-game has own RAF.

Rewards:
- On finish: compute quality (0..100) based on perfect and misses. Award girls' mood/history and `outsidePlayBonus`, focus/temper, set `sandboxPlayed=true`, maybe a visible castle in the yard for the rest of the visit. Display result screen with stats and a "Back to the yard" button.
- Perfect castle can give extra: a "sandcastle masterpiece" that adds a keepsake or bonus? Maybe a heart from girls and a group photo. Keep simple but meaningful.
- Natural consequence: If the player rushes or misses, the quality is low and reward lower, possibly one girl loses interest (mood drop) and no cooperation boost. This makes the timing skill meaningful.
- Also connect to household: success adds `outsidePlayBonus` and mood/history; maybe perfect adds an extra boost. Low quality maybe still small boost.

On-canvas visuals: Draw sky gradient, ocean waves with animated sine, sand, castle with tiers, flag, girls sitting around? Could draw simple emoji? Better draw shapes. A moving sand-meter: horizontal bar at bottom with moving marker and green center. Tap anywhere / space. Show "Tap when the bucket is over the green patch" with 5 buckets. Animation: a bucket moves side to side along a rail; the green patch is centered or random position. Each tap scores based on distance. Hmm, for tap-timing, a swinging bucket over a target zone. Let's design:

- There's a "packing beam" with a pointer sliding left-right at speed increasing each round. Target zone in middle-ish (randomized each level but with some margin). Tap/click/Space to stop.
- The bucket drops sand at the stop point. If within green zone => perfect (adds a level, +20 quality). Yellow zone => okay (+10). Outside => spill (+0 and maybe -5 quality/one attempt wasted).
- 5 total drops. Show progress with 5 bucket icons or pips. The castle grows visually after each drop.
- Use fixed ~1.8s per sweep, speed increasing.
- On mobile, big button "Drop the sand" under canvas in addition to tap. Actually tapping canvas itself is big enough; add button.
- Need to avoid ghost taps / start interactions. Add pointerdown listener; also keydown when active. Maybe prevent B and E keys while mini-game active: keydown handler currently catches B/E globally. Add guard in global keydown: if miniGameActive, route keys (Space/Enter) to mini-game and return. Also openDadBreak should be blocked while mini-game active. Add early return.

### Fetch mini-game (throw-and-chase)
Visual: side view? Top-down yard with Dad and Charlie. The player aims a throw by pressing/holding a power meter and setting direction. Then Charlie chases the ball along the yard and brings it back; timing/aiming affects success. Could be interactive in stages:
1. Aim: a reticle sweeps across the yard; tap to set direction (or choose distance with a moving power bar).
2. Throw: ball arcs to the spot. Charlie runs to it. The closer the throw lands to a marked "sweet spot" / within the yard and away from obstacles, the better Charlie's fetch rating. If thrown into the sandbox, flowerbed, or gate, Charlie gets distracted / it's a poor throw.
3. Return: Charlie runs back; tap at the right moment to praise him? Simpler: 3 rounds; each round has aim+power via two-click timing. Use a single moving marker: a target ring oscillates over distance and lateral aim? Hmm.

Maybe design as a top-down mini-game with controls:
- Dad at bottom center, Charlie at bottom right. A ball trajectory reticle (crosshair) moves across the yard in a figure-eight or side-to-side pattern. A power/distance meter fills and loops. Click once to lock the throw's landing spot (reticle) and distance? Two-dimensional aim with one click is tricky.
- Alternative: a "throw meter" with three zones (short/perfect/long) and direction fixed toward the open lawn; tap to stop the moving power indicator at the perfect zone. Then Charlie chases the ball automatically; a "cheer" timing window appears when he's returning, and tapping in the green zone makes him sprint back happily. 3 rounds. This is more rhythm/timing than throwing. But could be satisfying with animated Charlie fetching.

Let's design richer fetch:
- Phase "aim": A target ring sweeps left-right across the lawn (X position); tap to lock horizontal landing X. Then phase "power": a vertical/horizontal power bar oscillates; tap to lock power (distance). The ball then arcs from Dad to (x, y=distance). If it lands on the "good grass" (big central region) = good. If near the sandbox = Charlie digs instead (fun but lower score). If too close = "barely a toss". If beyond fence = lost ball / wasted.
- Phase "chase": Charlie runs toward the ball, picks it up, runs back. A praise timing bar appears when he's halfway back? Tapping when the ring aligns gives a "Good boy!" bonus. 3 rounds, with score: distance accuracy + praise.

  - Keyboard fallback: arrow keys aim? Complex. Use Space to throw with oscillating aim? Hmm, tests can use debug API, but accessibility/desktop users need something. Simpler: For keyboard, the aim ring sweeps automatically and Space throws at current aim; drag optional for mouse/touch. But mixing is odd.

Maybe a single unified timing mechanism with a visual "throw arc" preview:
- A target reticle slides left-right across the yard automatically, and a power bar oscillates. Click once to throw at the reticle position with current power. That's one click. Then Charlie chases. Actually let's not over-engineer. Requirements: "throw-and-chase fetch game with Charlie". The core fantasy: throw ball, Charlie chases, bring back. We can make aim a moving reticle and power fixed to a "perfect" distance? Or click to set target and Charlie chases. Let's set the fetch mini-game:

A green target zone (target band) appears on the bar corresponding to the ring's distance, width ~18. Player presses/taps "Throw!" or Space to release. Accuracy = closeness to zone center. messages.summary:
## Objective
- Continue adding interactive backyard mini-games to the household parenting RPG, starting with sandcastle building and fetch.

## Requirements
- Preserve existing household routines, Charlie behavior, yard mechanics, parenting choices, Dad breaks, and mobile controls.
- Make outdoor activities visually and interactively playable with consequences that affect mood, stress, focus, patience, cooperation, and household gameplay.

<subagent sessionID="ses_df7b66291ffeoDPctBmj2YQ9zY" state="completed">
## Findings

### Charlie rendering and movement
- Charlie is drawn as a side-on, fixed-size ellipsoid regardless of activity; no distinct nap, sitting, crouching, or wake pose exists (`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html:234-235`).
- Nap behavior is visualized only by the agenda and `Zzz…` bubble. Charlie remains in the same rendered orientation while stationary (`:397-400`).
- Charlie has an initial coordinate and `Great Pyrenees` metadata, but no animation state for walking, sitting, or lying down. Movement only changes his position (`:139`, `:234-235`, `:377-379`).
- Yard Charlie is larger only in conceptual context, not postured differently (`:276`).

### Realism and nap placement
- Nap destinations include hallways, bedroom areas, the living room, and [560,520], which appears near the kitchen/living boundary (`:397`, `:377-378`).
- The stored agenda can say “napping in a doorway,” and several destinations are doorway-adjacent. This creates the intentional blocking hazard, but is poor dog-sleep placement from a realism perspective.
- Wake-up sends Charlie to random preset locations, but there is no visual indication of a destination or reason for it (`:315`).
- The test’s forced hallway nap at [477,350] and trip reaction are consistent with the implementation, but do not assess physical plausibility (`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/tests/charlie-nap-test.js:15-57`).
- Charlie collision is implemented by preventing girls and Dad from occupying his position, while movement allows Charlie to startle and relocate (`index.html:377-378`, `:387`).

### Couch/sitting feasibility
- There is no couch or sofa prop in the house furniture list (`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html:105-123`).
- The room contains a TV, toys, and books, but no visible seating other than dining chairs and beds (`:118-120`, `:215-222`).
- `seatedAtTable` tracks meal seating only; it does not control a sitting pose or furniture position (`:380`).
- Every human character is rendered as the same upright body regardless of sleeping or sitting:
  - Girls remain standing while `asleep` is set after reaching beds (`:380`, `:234-235`).
  - Dad is the only character with a distinct asleep pose (`:234-235`).
- Therefore, a couch-sitting feature is not blocked by a complex existing actor system, but it would require all of: a couch prop, a destination/route state, a `sitting` agenda, and a separate couch-pose drawing branch.

### Existing test coverage
- The nap test covers stationary napping, collision/tripping, Dad wake-up interaction, movement after waking, and JavaScript page errors (`charlie-nap-test.js:15-74`, `:76`).
- The yard test covers fencing, patrol movement, car barking, sandbox use, fetch, reward limits, and yard resets (`yard-purpose-test.js:41-75`, `:78-175`).
- There is no dedicated test or code path for couch, sofa, sitting, lying-down, or furniture-capacity behavior.
- Wake tests verify only that Charlie gains a route or changes state; they do not validate the destination, clear use of the space, or animated posture (`charlie-nap-test.js:59-74`).

## Recommendations
1. Add a couch prop to the living room and give it explicit sit coordinates and capacity.
2. Introduce actor posture states: `standing`, `walking`, `sitting`, `lying`, and `asleep`, rather than changing only `bubble` or `agenda`.
3. Draw Charlie lying on his side or curled for naps, and use a seated pose at the couch. Use a separate pose while walking.
4. Replace doorway nap selection with explicit safe locations: a designated pet bed/rug or a resting area away from doors and foot traffic.
5. Mark chairs/beds/couch positions with collision or occupancy data so actors cannot overlap furniture incorrectly.
6. Add tests for:
   - Charlie moves to the dedicated nap location.
   - Charlie lies down and resumes a standing pose when waking.
   - Couch sitting is visible and stays within couch bounds.
   - People cannot occupy the same couch or dog-bed spot.
   - Wake-up and sit-to-walk transitions leave no stale route or pose state.
- No files were modified.
</subagent>

<subagent sessionID="ses_df7a6e0cbffeKkGGXdFDX3LTeq" state="completed" description="Map tests and controls">
## Test layout

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/tests/run.js`
  - Starts `python3 -m http.server` on `PORT`/`3002`.
  - Waits for `/index.html`.
  - Sets `BASE_URL`.
  - Runs, in order:
    - `tests/playtest.js`
    - `tests/mechanics-test.js`
    - `tests/charlie-nap-test.js`
    - `tests/opening-break-test.js`
    - `tests/yard-test.js`
    - `tests/yard-purpose-test.js`
    - `tests/mobile-test.js`
  - Continues after failures, exits nonzero, and always stops the server.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/tests/browser.js`
  - Locates an installed Chromium/Playwright executable.
  - Falls back to the environment Playwright-Core installation.
  - Exports `launch()` for headless tests.

## Common test patterns

- Use Playwright via `tests/browser.js`.
- Navigate to `/index.html?debug=1&v=<timestamp>` to enable the debug API and bypass stale caches.
- Start the game, wait for `window.__game` and `opening === false`, then close the opening dialog if necessary.
- Capture `pageerror` and console errors.
- Use direct DOM helpers for dialog title/buttons and use `.click()` for deterministic choices.
- Place Dad or NPCs at exact coordinates through `__game.player` or `__game.girls`.
- Accelerate NPCs or directly set routes to avoid timing/flakiness.
- Prefer `waitForFunction` and bounded polling over fixed delays.
- Tests throw `ASSERT FAILED`/`ASSERT` errors and print passing checks; they do not use Jest/Mocha.

## Debug API

Exposed as `window.__game` only when `?debug=1` is present.

State/hooks include:

- State setters: `setTemper`, `setFocus`, `setBreak`, `setScene`, `setWash`, `setOpening`
- NPC/task control: `girls`, `tasks`, `player`, `charlieTimer`, `callGirls`, `sendGirlToTask`, `completeTask`, `respond`, `redirectGirl`
- Movement and interaction: `interact`, `roomAt`, `setDestination`, `setMultiDestination`, `routeArrived`
- Dialogs: `openDialog`, `closeDialog`
- Outdoor: `goOutside`, `goInside`, `callGirlsOutside`, `sendGirlsInside`, `assignYardPlay`
- Mini-games: `miniState`, `miniPrimary`, `miniAim`, `startSandcastleGame`, `startFetchGame`, `closeMiniGame`
- Yard/fetch/sandbox actions: `playInSandbox`, `playFetch`, `spawnCar`
- Laundry/shower helpers: `startShowerSequence`, `handleShowerInteraction`, `openLaundryDialog`, `requestLaundryHelp`, `delegateTask`
- Other interaction helpers: `promptGirlMove`, `cheerGirl`, `handleYardInteract`, `offerTaskParenting`, `showerParenting`

State snapshots expose temper/focus/time, opening/pause/win state, task cycle timers, scene and yard state, Charlie/cars, outdoor activity counters, and mini-game state.

## Commands

```sh
npm install
npm test
npm run serve
```

Package scripts:

- `npm test` — full managed suite.
- `npm run test:playtest` — requires a server already running.
- `npm run test:mechanics` — requires a server already running.

Direct focused tests:

```sh
BASE_URL=http://localhost:3002 node tests/charlie-nap-test.js
BASE_URL=http://localhost:3002 node tests/opening-break-test.js
BASE_URL=http://localhost:3002 node tests/yard-test.js
BASE_URL=http://localhost:3002 node tests/yard-purpose-test.js
BASE_URL=http://localhost:3002 node tests/mobile-test.js
BASE_URL=http://localhost:3002 node tests/mechanics-test.js
BASE_URL=http://localhost:3002 node tests/playtest.js
```

With no server, start `npm run serve` first. `tests/run.js` uses `PORT` for an alternate server port.

## Relevant existing coverage

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/tests/playtest.js`
  - Full-day flow, refusal/redirection, seating, showers, laundry, meals, Charlie zoomies/proximity, bedtime, and win state.
  - Also asserts uncaught page and console errors.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/tests/mechanics-test.js`
  - Coffee focus/cooldown, dad breaks/cooldowns, and temper drain under non-compliance.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/tests/charlie-nap-test.js`
  - Nap stationarity, NPC collision avoidance/tripping, and Dad waking Charlie.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/tests/opening-break-test.js`
  - Opening wake dialog, break/push-through paths, dialog restoration, and wake safety net.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/tests/yard-test.js`
  - Outdoor transition, decline/accept flows, girls and Charlie returning, and action interactions.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/tests/yard-purpose-test.js`
  - Fresh-air rewards, anti-farming, Charlie patrol/car bark, yard spreading, sandbox/fetch limits, and indoor reset behavior.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/tests/mobile-test.js`
  - Portrait/landscape touch layouts, viewport overflow, movement pad, action button, sidebar scrolling, and break UI.

## Recommended focused checkpoint tests

1. Charlie nap requirements: `charlie-nap-test.js`.
   - Especially verify stationary nap behavior, no collision, trip wake reaction, and wake dialog.
2. Opening and dad-break requirements: `opening-break-test.js` plus `mechanics-test.js`.
   - Verify wake dialog recovery and break/cooldown/focus/temper behavior.
3. Yard requirements: `yard-purpose-test.js`, followed by `yard-test.js`.
   - Verify fresh-air benefits, once-per-visit boosts, sandbox/fetch caps, yard movement, car barking, and reset on return inside.
4. Mobile requirement: `mobile-test.js`.
   - Run at 844×390 and 390×844; verify no overflow, touch movement/action/break, and sidebar scroll.
5. If checkpoint is end-to-end flow: `playtest.js`.
   - It is the strongest verification of task ordering, win state, NPC behavior, dialogs, and uncaught errors.
6. Final regression: `npm test`.
   - This is the authoritative aggregate command but the individual scripts are faster for diagnosing a specific checkpoint.
</subagent>

- Finish and verify the household and backyard game improvements.

- Preserve the kitchen/bathroom divider `[332,397,332,670]`, living-room doorway `y=315–385`, hallway waypoints `[646,350]` and `[684,350]`, couch footprint `{x:690,y:430,w:180,h:78}`, substantial furniture blocking, couch seating, Charlie nap behavior, collision-aware routing, sandcastle/fetch gameplay, rewards, visit caps, and selective labels.

- Keep couch destinations outside the couch footprint.
- Assign couch mode to the first girl sent for afternoon activity.
